title: BotDojo Launch: Enhancing AI Assistants with Evaluations and Synthetic Data

primary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
primary.rationale: The talk centers on batch evaluations detecting knowledge gaps and hallucinations, with synthetic data generation used to improve measured chatbot performance in a support domain.

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The talk centers on batch evaluations detecting knowledge gaps and hallucinations, with synthetic data generation used to improve measured chatbot performance in a support domain.

summary: Paul Henry introduces BotDojo, an AI enablement platform designed to help companies confidently deploy LLM applications to production. Drawing from his experience as former CTO of Auctane, where he led engineering through growth from 10 to 2,000 employees, Paul addresses the gap between prototyping LLM apps (easy to do over a weekend) and making them production-ready. The live demo centers on combining synthetic data generation with evaluations to improve a support chatbot. Paul first demonstrates a battle-tested chatbot template that retrieves information from a vector database, showing the low-code editor with node-level execution traces that reveal exactly what was sent to the LLM and what came from the retriever. The platform supports JSON schema output for models like Grok and Claude. He then shows BotDojo's batches feature, which runs many questions through a chatbot and applies evaluations checking for knowledge gaps and hallucinations. The initial batch shows some failures (red results) due to insufficient vector database information. To fix this, Paul demonstrates a synthetic data generation flow that extracts questions and answers from support ticket interactions with live agents, uses relevant information from the existing index to write new documents in a matching style, performs an inline evaluation to verify the document has enough information to answer the question, and writes the result to the vector index. Code nodes support TypeScript with Python coming soon. After re-running the batch with the generated data included, the comparison shows all-green results, indicating improvement.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.
temporalContext: Transcript claims reflect the publication date; linked external context was checked at the run's research date.
takeaways: BotDojo is an AI enablement platform covering the full lifecycle from design and evaluation to deployment of LLM applications

Inline evaluations verify generated documents contain enough information to answer target questions before adding to the vector index

sections.title: Introduction and Background
sections.summary: Paul Henry introduces himself as founder of BotDojo and former CTO of Auctane, noting the gap between easy LLM prototyping and production readiness, positioning BotDojo as an AI enablement company.

sections.title: Chatbot Template Demo
sections.summary: Paul demonstrates a battle-tested support chatbot template, showing node-level execution, the low-code editor with prompt configuration, JSON schema support, and trace debugging capabilities.

sections.title: Batch Evaluations
sections.summary: Paul shows the batches feature running multiple questions through the chatbot with evaluations, revealing red results caused by insufficient vector database information and hallucination checks.

sections.title: Synthetic Data Generation Flow
sections.summary: Paul demonstrates a flow that extracts Q&A from support tickets, uses existing index information to write documents in matching style, runs inline evaluations to verify sufficient information, and writes to the vector index. Code nodes support TypeScript with Python coming soon.

sections.title: Final Comparison and Results
sections.summary: After a tense moment with technical difficulties, Paul compares the before-and-after batch results, showing all-green results indicating improvement from the synthetic data. He mentions BotDojo is hiring AI engineers and directs people to botdojo.com.

demonstrations: Running a support chatbot template that retrieves from a vector database and answers using an LLM
Inspecting node-level traces showing exact data sent to LLM and retrieved from vector database
Viewing the prompt and JSON schema configuration in the low-code editor
Running batch evaluations on a chatbot across multiple questions, showing red results for knowledge gaps
Cloning and re-running a batch with generated data included by removing a filter
Running a synthetic data generation flow that takes JSON input from support ticket Q&A pairs
Generating documents in matching style from existing index information with inline evaluation
Writing generated documents to the vector index via a code node
Comparing before-and-after batch results showing all-green after synthetic data addition
limitations: Paul did not have enough time to generate all data for the demo live, so pre-generated data was used by removing a filter
The demo had technical difficulty during the final batch comparison (failed multiple times before succeeding)
Code nodes do not yet support Python (TypeScript only currently)
quantitativeClaims: Paul led Auctane's growth from 10 to 2,000 employees
Auctane's logistics platform processes over three billion orders annually for more than a million customers
Initial batch evaluation showed 5 evaluations with some red results
Final batch comparison showed all-green results after adding synthetic data
